title: Muse Launches Open Source Gadgets SDK and 5000 Free Home Link Devices
summary:
The Muse Home Link device allows the Muse AI to interact with a user's television or speakers by connecting to a home network via USB-C and using HTTPS. Alongside this hardware, Nat Friedman released Muse Gadgets, which consists of open source ESP32 firmware and a Linux SDK designed to enable developers to build their own compatible peripherals.

Muse produced a limited batch of 5,000 Home Link units that will ship in a few weeks and are available for free to current subscribers while supplies last. To facilitate third-party hardware development, the company has open sourced the Home Link code and provided API tokens and a GitHub repository.

We built a gadget of our own, too: Muse Home Link is a little usb-c powered device that allows Muse to connect to your home network to talk to smart home devices like TVs and speakers and anything else that exposes https.

We manufactured a batch of 5000 Home Links which should be ready to ship in a few weeks, and they are free for Muse subscribers while supplies last. Claim yours at https://t.co/Q0dE0cYnCs

All the code for Muse Home Link is open source too!
